title: Transporting Quantiles to Codebook: Scalable Vector Quantization without Codebook Collapse
claim: A fixed, well-behaved prior codebase is transported by a learned flow, then refined, into a density-adaptive codebook.
layout: 5 stages, left-to-right, encoder→prior→zoom→posterior→decoder, red flow arc on top
description: A horizontal pipeline runs left to right. A small neural network (E_θ) feeds a gray latent block. An arrow leads to a square 2D panel labeled C_0, the prior codebook. It shows white dots (codes) on a Voronoi partition with a blue density haze, dense at the center, and a red cluster of samples. A large red arc labeled ψ₁^γ sweeps over the top to a second panel, C_1, the posterior codebook. There the codes and Voronoi cells follow three blue density modes. A circular dashed zoom in the middle, labeled self-correction (C_1, S_1), shows a white code moving toward the centroid of red samples. Z_q and z_e are marked in the posterior panel. A red latent block then connects to a decoder network (D_θ). The red arc draws the eye first.
caption: FlowVQ on a three-mode 2D latent distribution (K = 50): the learned flow $\psi^\gamma_1$ transports the approximately equal-mass quantile prior codebook $\mathcal{C}_0 \in \mathcal{N}(0, I)$, initialized using Sobol samples here and kept fixed thereafter, to the latent space. Self-correction refines each transported code using the pushed quantile samples $\mathcal{S}_1$, yielding the density-adaptive posterior codebook $\mathcal{C}_1$.
abstract: Effective discrete representation learning with VQ-VAE serves as a fundamental component of modern autoregressive generative models. However, it is widely known to suffer from codebook collapse and inefficient code utilization. To address this issue, we propose FlowVQ, a simple yet effective alternative to standard vector quantization by formulating neural quantization as a joint modeling and clustering process. Specifically, we learn the latent space using a lightweight flow matching model alongside training, corresponding to a probability flow ODE that transports an often fixed well-behaved source distribution while preserving probability mass. Based on this, we define the codebook C_1 by transporting even-quantile partitioned prior codes C_0 from the source space through the learned flow, and obtaining the Voronoi centroids under the induced distribution, leading to a structured discretization. We evaluated on image tokenization and generation, as well as on two tasks requiring high-precision tokenization, demonstrating scalability and improved expressivity of the codebook with full utilization.
